name: blender beginner setup navigation and geometry practice
goal: Start Blender the right way: Layout workspace focus, three-button mouse nav, G/S/R, Edit mode verts/edges/faces, then freeform practice.

source.title: Watch This Before you Get Started with Blender (7 Tips)

inputs.name: learning_goal
inputs.description: End goal for your Blender learning map

outputs.name: practice_meshes
outputs.description: Experimental meshes from G/S/R and Edit mode practice

constraints: Start on Layout workspace; ignore Outliner/Properties/Timeline at first
Prefer MMB nav over toolbar zoom/pan/orbit icons
Navigate in small increments to avoid overshooting
Delete with Shift+X then Enter (as taught in this video)

steps.action: Write a short learning map: end goal plus key concepts/procedures to learn (skip unrelated tutorials).
Open Blender; select Layout workspace; mentally ignore top menus, Outliner, Properties, Timeline—focus on 3D Viewport and default cube.
Use a three-button mouse: scroll zoom; MMB drag orbit; Shift+MMB pan. Practice small incremental orbits from screen center.
Object mode: G grab/move, S scale, R rotate the cube; click to confirm.
Tab into Edit mode. Selection modes: 1 vertex, 2 edge, 3 face. G/R/S components; Shift-click or box-select (wireframe for through-select).
Tab to Object mode; Shift+A → Mesh to add primitives at the 3D cursor; G to place; edit in Edit mode.
Delete extras in Object mode with Shift+X, Enter. Build rough recognizable shapes without tutorials to cement fundamentals.

verification: Can toggle Edit mode and select vert/edge/face
